subject: Accounting
title: Document Examination
description: A micro-lesson that makes Document Examination usable.

hook.text: The invoice looks real—right logo, right format. But the phone number goes to a burner phone.

buildup.text: Document examination scrutinizes invoices, contracts, and receipts for signs of forgery or fabrication.

discovery.text: Red flags include mismatched fonts, sequential invoice numbers from different vendors, and P.O. box addresses.

twist.text: Modern printers and software make forgery easier—but metadata in digital files often reveals the truth.

climax.text: Comparing documents against known authentic samples and cross-referencing with third parties uncovers fakes.

punchline.text: A document that looks right can still be very wrong.

quiz.question: What is a red flag when examining invoices?
options: Sequential numbers from supposedly different vendors

details.summary: Document examination in forensic accounting involves analyzing financial records—invoices, checks, contracts, and ledgers—for signs of alteration, forgery, or fabrication. This topic covers the techniques used to verify document authenticity and detect manipulation.
details.whyItMatters: Forged or altered documents are at the heart of most financial fraud schemes. The ability to detect fabricated evidence separates successful investigations from failed ones.
takeaways: Examinations check for altered dates, amounts, signatures, and terms on financial documents
Digital forensics can detect PDF modifications, metadata inconsistencies, and image manipulation
Chain of custody must be maintained for examined documents to be admissible as evidence in court

faq.question: How do forensic accountants examine documents for fraud?
faq.answer: They look for physical signs of alteration (different ink, whiteout, misaligned text), verify signatures against known samples, check document metadata for inconsistencies, compare details across related documents, and verify that invoices and contracts match actual business activity.

faq.question: Can digitally created documents be verified?
faq.answer: Yes. Digital forensics examines file metadata (creation date, modification history, author), checks for image editing artifacts, verifies email headers and routing, and compares file properties against claimed provenance. Even PDFs carry hidden metadata that reveals their history.
